clue.text: Eton chap shambles along Whitehall, a sad reminder

indicators.note: to shamble is to walk awkwardly, so the letters of Eton chap stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A public schoolboy shuffles down Whitehall past a sombre monument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cenotaph is the war memorial on Whitehall, the London street of government offices, where Remembrance Sunday is held.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cenotaph is London's national war memorial, standing in Whitehall as a solemn reminder of the dead.

clue.text: Dutch produce early English green beans

parts.note: Edam is a cheese made in the Netherlands
AM, ante meridiem, the morning hours

explanation.surface: Dutch growers produce green beans ahead of the English season.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young soybeans eaten still in the pod, a green vegetable popular as a snack.

clue.text: 10s the end of many Russian women?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gametes, the answer to 10 across; female ones are eggs

definitions.text: the end of many Russian women?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the feminine ending of Russian surnames such as Ivanova

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 10 across gives GAMETE; the plural female kind are eggs. The question mark flags the playful second reading about surname endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova are egg cells, the female reproductive cells, and -ova closes many Russian women's family names.

clue.text: Not having the front seat on a tandem's rotten

indicators.note: the word loses its front, its opening letter

parts.note: a bicycle seat is a saddle

explanation.surface: The back rider on a tandem complains the front seat is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled egg is a rotten one, gone bad and unfit to eat.

clue.text: Comedian's article Charlie pawned?

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s is short for 'is', so the clue reads Comedian is: the definition is the noun alone, a single person

indicators.note: the question mark tells the solver to read pawned as the phrase 'in hock', whose 'in' puts the other pieces inside

parts.note: goods that are pawned are said to be in hock
an is the indefinite article
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A comic's belongings, Charlie's included, have been taken to the pawnbroker.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that pawned means 'in hock', so the article and Charlie sit in HOCK; the question mark owns up to the stretch. Tony Hancock was a much-loved British comedian of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Hancock was a famous British radio and television comic, star of Hancock's Half Hour.

clue.text: Sleepy-looking father of three girls cleared out baby clothes

indicators.note: used as a verb: the outer pair dress the father, holding him inside
the inside of baby is emptied, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: King Lear has three daughters, Goneril, Regan and Cordelia

explanation.surface: A tired dad of three daughters has thrown out the baby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun after 'baby', but it is a verb meaning dresses or wraps around. Lear is Shakespeare's king with three daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and watery from tiredness, so a bleary person looks half asleep.

clue.text: I'm used to rising damp

parts.note: rising damp is a building's moisture problem; here it is someone who habitually wakes up wet

explanation.walkthrough: Rising damp is a house complaint, but 'rising' here means getting out of bed, damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedwetter is a person, usually a child, who urinates in bed at night and so wakes wet.

clue.text: In heaven I relax — death isn't normally structured

indicators.note: the letters are not in their normal structure, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dying person feels at ease, finding death not what they had pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in heaven is an idiom for being overjoyed, which is what exhilarated means.

clue.text: Carpet salesman set off without an itinerary

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rove is to wander with no fixed route

explanation.surface: A carpet salesman sets out on his rounds with no plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like the salesman's stock, but it is a verb: to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called in and scolded by a superior, which is to be reproved.

clue.text: Mum stops swim after Jack and I jumped in the sea

indicators.note: the swim part comes after the sailor and the rest

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
I as a numeral is one

indicators.note: the quiet sign stops up the swim, sitting inside it

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
mum's the word: keep quiet, SH

explanation.surface: A sailor and I leapt overboard while Mum stopped us swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning ship means leaving a sinking vessel, often by leaping overboard into the water.

clue.text: Maybe sperm whales eat veg regularly

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: taking every other letter at a steady interval

explanation.surface: Sperm whales, perhaps, munch their greens on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sperm whales' reads as one creature, but 'Maybe sperm' is the definition and 'whales' starts the wordplay. ETE is every other letter of eat veg.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm cell is an example of a reproductive cell, the male kind, alongside the egg.

clue.text: Deporting criminals is no longer the done thing

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
a tradition is the customary thing to do

explanation.surface: Sending criminals abroad has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is handing over an accused person to another country to face trial there.

clue.text: Discount place for a cistern opening in Knightsbridge

parts.note: an old-style cistern sits above the toilet, over the loo

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A plumber offers a discount on a cistern for a posh London flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for toilet. Knightsbridge is a wealthy London district.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount something is to disregard it, which is to overlook it.

clue.text: Tinder for one lunch with an evangelist? Satisfied all round

indicators.note: the first word goes all the way around the others

parts.note: met as in met a demand
to lunch is to eat
Mark wrote one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: A dating app match leads to lunch with a preacher, and everyone leaves happy.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat market is slang for a place where people seek casual partners, and the dating app Tinder is an example.

clue.text: Anyone wanting to play cello with arms flailing?

indicators.note: arms flailing wildly are thrown about, as these letters are

explanation.surface: Who'd like a go at the cello, waving their arms about?
explanation.definitionFit: All-comers are everyone who chooses to enter a contest, open to any player.

clue.text: A little vibrator was liberating with fellow away

indicators.note: the fellow is sent off from the word

parts.note: freed, having set loose
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A small sex toy felt freeing once the man had left.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is the thin strip in a woodwind mouthpiece that vibrates to make the sound.

clue.text: Skin last seal in the Atlantic, perhaps

indicators.note: to skin is to strip off the outside, leaving each word's inner letters

explanation.surface: A hunter skins the final seal caught in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Asea means at sea, out on the water, and the Atlantic is an example of a sea.

clue.text: Not inclined to lie after studying the Ten Commandments etc.

parts.note: since in the sense of after a time
RE, religious education, the school subject

explanation.surface: Having learned the Ten Commandments, someone has given up lying.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is honest and genuine, not given to deceit.

clue.text: American volume a new collection of true stories

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre

indicators.note: a fresh collection of these letters is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A US book offers a fresh anthology of real-life tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection of true stories' looks like the definition, but only 'stories' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is written work, including novels and other fiction told as tales.

clue.text: What's brown and sticky? Bit of wood a canine left inside

indicators.note: these letters are placed within the tree

parts.note: a wood is made of trees, so one tree is a bit of it
C is the dental notation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: An old riddle, then a dog that has left its mark inside a bit of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The classic joke answer to 'What's brown and sticky?' is 'a stick'. Treacle is British for molasses or golden syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick dark syrup from sugar refining, both dark-coloured and gluey.

clue.text: Hit on a nerd for a change

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with a geek just to try something different.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear-end a vehicle is to crash into it from behind.

clue.text: Good parts not for me? A tragedy

indicators.note: the letter separates, parting, the words around it

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour of
one is a way to refer to oneself

explanation.surface: An actor turns down the good roles, saying the tragedy isn't for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like theatre roles, but it is a verb: G divides ANTI from ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is the Greek tragedy by Sophocles about the daughter of Oedipus.

clue.text: University's preparation for teaching strike chaos

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a degree that trains teachers
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A teacher-training course is thrown into disorder by a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action but means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London madhouse, means a scene of uproar and confusion.

clue.text: One speaking for the Foreign Office sent over generous offer

indicators.note: sent over turns the letters back to front

parts.words: One speaking for the Foreign Office
parts.note: the Foreign Office's mouth, FO plus gob, slang for mouth: its mouthpiece

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for the Foreign Office relays a generous deal abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: BOGOF is British shop slang for 'buy one, get one free'.
explanation.definitionFit: A buy-one-get-one-free deal gives shoppers a second item at no cost, a bountiful promotion.

clue.text: Unofficial power supply in emergencies

indicators.note: read as supple-y, bending flexibly, so the letters are pliable and rearranged

explanation.surface: A backup generator supplies electricity when crises strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power supply' reads as electricity, but 'supply' is the anagram signal, read as 'in a supple way'.
explanation.definitionFit: An éminence grise is a person who wields influence behind the scenes without holding office.

clue.text: Jack's companion is missing Jack badly

indicators.note: the companion is lacking the letter that follows

parts.note: Jack and Jill went up the hill in the nursery rhyme
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: Jill misses Jack terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as an adverb means poorly, as in ill-advised or ill thought out.

clue.text: On reflection, it's wrong to trap game

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things back to front

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a net traps fish or game

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, it's unfair to snare game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' sits next to 'trap' as if it were quarry to be caught; it is the definition, a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played on a court, one example of a game.

clue.text: Some back-pedal if near the firing line

indicators.note: the letters are read from back to front
only some of the letters in these words are taken

explanation.surface: A cyclist backs off as they approach the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' does double duty in back-pedal: it turns round the letters hidden in 'pedal if near'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfilade is gunfire raking a line of troops from end to end, so it is a line of fire.
